charts.name: donut_density
charts.title: Auckland: people per hectare
charts.source: Stats NZ 2013 and 2023 Census usually resident population counts
charts.note: Auckland urban area, grouped into 2 km bands by straight-line distance from Britomart to each area's centre point. Land excludes water. The teal top of each bar is the increase from 2013 to 2023.

charts.name: donut_share
charts.title: Auckland: where the people added went
charts.source: Stats NZ 2013 and 2023 Census usually resident population counts
charts.note: Each 2 km band's share of the urban area's 2013 residents, and of the net number of people added by 2023. Areas that lost people count against their band.

charts.name: donut_pace
charts.title: Auckland: growth a year by distance
charts.source: Stats NZ 2013 and 2023 Census usually resident population counts
charts.note: Average yearly growth in residents between the March 2013 and March 2023 Censuses, compared with the urban area as a whole. Bands far out start from few people, so their rates run high.

charts.name: donut_bands
charts.title: Auckland: residents and new homes
charts.source: Stats NZ building consents and 2023 Census
charts.note: Shares by 2 km distance band from Britomart. Consents since 2016; population is the 2023 Census count. Consents are permissions, not completions.

charts.name: donut_curve
charts.title: Auckland: where homes were consented
charts.source: Stats NZ building consents and 2023 Census
charts.note: Cumulative shares ordered by distance. Below the diagonal means consents lie further out relative to 2023 residents. The period comparison is descriptive, not a policy-effect estimate.

charts.name: donut_lorenz
charts.title: Auckland: how evenly growth was shared
charts.source: Stats NZ 2013 and 2023 Census usually resident population counts
charts.note: Auckland urban areas, ordered from Britomart outwards. The line adds up each area's share of 2013 residents and of population growth from 2013 to 2023. On the dashed line, growth would follow where people already lived. The further the line sits below it, the more growth went to outer areas. The Gini coefficient measures that gap: 0 is even, and higher means more growth further out. Areas that lost people pull the line down, so it can dip below zero.

charts.name: donut_rates
charts.title: Auckland: new homes per 100 residents
charts.source: Stats NZ building consents and 2023 Census
charts.note: Consents since 2016 by dwelling type and distance band. Rates exclude areas below 100 residents; totals retain them. Townhouses includes flats, units and other dwellings.

charts.name: donut_growth
charts.title: Auckland: where new people and homes went
charts.source: Stats NZ building consents and 2013/2023 Censuses
charts.note: Shares of net population growth and new homes consented over the matching Census window. Areas that lost people contribute negative growth. Census counts are rounded and methods changed between censuses.

charts.name: hb1
charts.title: Exchange rates
charts.note: Shows how much foreign currency the New Zealand dollar buys. Use the selectors to compare currencies and the trade-weighted index.

charts.name: hb2
charts.title: Interest rates
charts.note: Tracks wholesale and retail borrowing rates. Select up to five series to compare changes in borrowing conditions over time.

charts.name: hc35
charts.title: Residential mortgages
charts.note: Shows mortgage lending across lending groups and loan types, providing context on household borrowing conditions.

charts.name: hm1
charts.title: Inflation
charts.note: Measures how prices change over time. Compare up to five headline or component price indexes using a common metric.

charts.name: hm2
charts.title: Consumption
charts.note: Describes household spending on goods and services—an important signal of demand and confidence in the economy.

charts.name: hm3
charts.title: Investment
charts.source: RBNZ and Stats NZ series · HM3
charts.note: Covers spending that builds future capacity. This view compares broad investment types.

charts.name: hm8
charts.title: Overseas trade
charts.note: Tracks the value and volume of goods and services bought from and sold to other countries.

charts.name: hm9
charts.title: Labour market
charts.note: Brings together employment, participation, hours and wages to show how work and earnings are changing.

charts.name: hm14
charts.title: Survey of expectations
charts.note: Summarises surveyed expectations for inflation and other economic measures. Expectations are opinions, not guaranteed forecasts.

charts.name: oecd_cpi
charts.title: Inflation compared
charts.note: Consumer prices, annual % change, quarterly. Compare published quarterly observations for New Zealand, Australia, Ireland, the UK, the US and the OECD total.

charts.name: fuel
charts.title: Jet fuel price
charts.note: Daily US Gulf Coast jet fuel spot price, a benchmark for airline fuel costs, in US dollars per barrel or New Zealand dollars per barrel at the RBNZ exchange rate.

charts.name: ndm01
charts.title: New dwelling completions
charts.note: Counts new homes completed each month in Ireland, by dwelling type.

charts.name: ect
charts.title: Card spending
charts.note: Compare monthly card spending by category in NZD millions or annual percent change; levels use seasonal adjustment where available.

charts.name: hm5
charts.title: Economic growth
charts.note: Compare real GDP growth, the current account as a share of GDP, the household saving rate, and annual changes in retail, wholesale and manufacturing sales, all in percent.

charts.name: yield
charts.title: Yield curve
charts.note: Compare up to four bond and swap rates or spreads. A negative spread means the first rate is lower than the second. Spreads are in basis points; rates are in percent.

charts.name: adp
charts.title: Accommodation
charts.note: Compare monthly domestic and international guest nights, occupancy and capacity utilisation for New Zealand or a regional tourism organisation.

charts.name: hs32
charts.title: Banks: loans by product
charts.note: Breaks registered-bank lending into products and borrower groups to show where credit is growing or contracting.

charts.name: bond
charts.title: Rental market
charts.note: Shows lodged, active and closed tenancy bonds and weekly rents by location, a direct read on the rental market.

charts.name: hm10
charts.title: CoreLogic
charts.note: Provides housing-market measures such as property values. Movements vary by place and do not represent every home.

charts.name: ie_labour
charts.title: Ireland: unemployment
charts.note: The share of the labour force out of work and looking for a job, in percent, seasonally adjusted. Compare age groups or men and women; the shaded area is everyone aged 15-74.

charts.name: ie_house_prices
charts.title: Ireland: house prices
charts.note: Monthly residential property prices for Ireland, Dublin and outside Dublin. Compare annual change in percent or the index (2015 = 100), for all dwellings, houses or apartments.

charts.name: ie_airports
charts.title: Ireland: airport passengers
charts.note: Passengers through Dublin, Cork, Shannon, Knock and Kerry airports each quarter. Compare the airports in passengers or against the same quarter of 2019, or see the annual % change.
